dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَعِنِّي عَلَى ذِكْرِكَ وَشُكْرِكَ وَحُسْنِ عِبَادَتِكَ
dua.transliteration: Allahumma a'inni 'ala dhikrika wa shukrika wa husni 'ibadatik
dua.english: O Allah, help me to remember You, be grateful to You, and worship You in the best manner.
dua.source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Sunan al-Nasa'i (sahih, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal RA)

verses.relevanceNote: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you — the promise of abundance through gratitude.
Remember Me, I will remember you. Be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.

days.tafsirFocus: Explore how gratitude (shukr) is the foundation of all worship and the beginning of a blessed Ramadan.
days.reflection: Begin your Ramadan by counting your blessings. What are three things you are grateful for today?

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْ عَمَلِي كُلَّهُ صَالِحًا، وَاجْعَلْهُ لِوَجْهِكَ خَالِصًا، وَلَا تَجْعَلْ لِأَحَدٍ فِيهِ شَيْئًا
dua.transliteration: Allahumma-j'al 'amali kullahu salihan, wa-j'alhu li-wajhika khalisan, wa la taj'al li-ahadin fihi shay'an
dua.english: O Allah, make all my deeds righteous, make them sincerely for Your sake, and let no one have any share in them.
dua.source: Sunan al-Tirmidhi (from Umar ibn al-Khattab RA)

verses.relevanceNote: They were commanded only to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion.
Worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, even though the disbelievers dislike it.

days.tafsirFocus: Understand ikhlas (sincerity) and how to purify your intentions during Ramadan.
days.reflection: Examine your intentions today. Are your acts of worship solely for Allah's pleasure?

dua.arabic: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَتُبْ عَلَيَّ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ
dua.transliteration: Rabbi-ghfir li wa tub 'alayya innaka Anta-t-Tawwab-ur-Rahim
dua.english: My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful.
dua.source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Sunan al-Tirmidhi (sahih, from Ibn Umar RA — the Prophet ﷺ would say this 100 times in a sitting)

verses.relevanceNote: Do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.
Turn to Allah in sincere repentance — your Lord may remove your misdeeds.

days.tafsirFocus: Learn about tawbah nasuh (sincere repentance) and Allah's infinite mercy.
days.reflection: What habits or sins do you need to repent from? Make sincere tawbah today.

dua.arabic: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا
dua.transliteration: Rabbana atina min ladunka rahmatan wa hayyi' lana min amrina rashada
dua.english: Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and prepare for us right guidance in our affair.
dua.source: Quran 18:10

verses.relevanceNote: My mercy encompasses all things — Allah's mercy is infinite.
Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy.

days.tafsirFocus: Understand Allah's attribute of Rahma and how to embody mercy toward others.
days.reflection: How can you show mercy to others today? Remember: the merciful receive mercy.

dua.arabic: رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا
dua.transliteration: Rabbana afrigh 'alayna sabran wa thabbit aqdamana
dua.english: Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet.
dua.source: Quran 2:250

verses.relevanceNote: O you who believe, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
The patient will be given their reward without account — unlimited reward for sabr.

days.tafsirFocus: Learn about the three types of sabr and how fasting trains us in patience.
days.reflection: Fasting is a school of patience. What challenges are testing your sabr today?

dua.arabic: حَسْبِيَ اللهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ
dua.transliteration: Hasbiya-Allahu la ilaha illa Huwa 'alayhi tawakkaltu
dua.english: Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. On Him I have relied.
dua.source: Quran 9:129

verses.relevanceNote: Whoever relies upon Allah — He is sufficient for him.
When you have decided, rely upon Allah. Allah loves those who rely upon Him.

days.tafsirFocus: Understand tawakkul as active trust, not passive resignation.
days.reflection: What worries are you carrying? Surrender them to Allah with complete trust.

dua.arabic: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيَّ الْقَيُّومَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ
dua.transliteration: Astaghfirullah-alladhi la ilaha illa Huwa-l-Hayya-l-Qayyuma wa atubu ilayh
dua.english: I seek forgiveness from Allah, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, and I repent to Him.
dua.source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Sunan al-Tirmidhi (sahih — whoever says it three times has their sins forgiven, even if they fled from battle)

verses.relevanceNote: Let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you?
The reward of an evil is an evil like it, but whoever pardons and makes reconciliation — his reward is from Allah.

days.tafsirFocus: Learn about 'afw (pardoning) vs. maghfirah (forgiveness) and their spiritual benefits.
days.reflection: Is there anyone you need to forgive? Liberation comes through letting go of grudges.

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أُشْرِكَ بِكَ وَأَنَا أَعْلَمُ، وَأَسْتَغْفِرُكَ لِمَا لَا أَعْلَمُ
dua.transliteration: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika an ushrika bika wa ana a'lam, wa astaghfiruka lima la a'lam
dua.english: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating partners with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know.
dua.source: Musnad Ahmad (sahih, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari RA)

verses.relevanceNote: The servants of the Most Merciful walk upon the earth in humility.
Do not turn your cheek in contempt toward people or walk through the earth exultantly.

days.tafsirFocus: Explore khushu (humility in worship) and tawadu (humility with people).
days.reflection: Fasting humbles the ego. How has hunger reminded you of your dependence on Allah?

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ، وَالْجُبْنِ وَالْبُخْلِ
dua.transliteration: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min al-'ajzi wal-kasali, wal-jubni wal-bukhli
dua.english: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from incapacity, laziness, cowardice, and miserliness.
dua.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim (from Anas ibn Malik RA)

verses.relevanceNote: The example of those who spend in the way of Allah is like a grain that produces seven spikes.
Those who give charity — it will be multiplied for them, and they will have a noble reward.

days.tafsirFocus: Learn about the spiritual purification that comes through giving.
days.reflection: The Prophet ﷺ was most generous in Ramadan. What can you give today — time, money, or kindness?

dua.arabic: رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا
dua.transliteration: Rabbi zidni 'ilma
dua.english: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.
dua.source: Quran 20:114

verses.relevanceNote: Read in the name of your Lord who created — the first revelation emphasizing knowledge.
Allah will raise those who have believed and those who were given knowledge by degrees.

days.tafsirFocus: The Quran was revealed in Ramadan. Focus on its lessons as the source of true knowledge.
days.reflection: What have you learned from the Quran this Ramadan? Set a goal to learn something new.

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَلِّفْ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِنَا، وَأَصْلِحْ ذَاتَ بَيْنِنَا، وَاهْدِنَا سُبُلَ السَّلَامِ
dua.transliteration: Allahumma allif bayna qulubina, wa aslih dhata bayinina, wa-hdina subul-as-salam
dua.english: O Allah, unite our hearts, reconcile our affairs, and guide us to the paths of peace.
dua.source: Sunan Abi Dawud (sahih)

verses.relevanceNote: The believers are but brothers, so make settlement between your brothers.
Hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided.

days.tafsirFocus: Explore the Islamic concept of ummah and brotherhood in faith.
days.reflection: Reach out to a fellow Muslim today. Strengthen the bonds of brotherhood.

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اكْفِنِي بِحَلَالِكَ عَنْ حَرَامِكَ، وَأَغْنِنِي بِفَضْلِكَ عَمَّنْ سِوَاكَ
dua.transliteration: Allahumma-kfini bi-halalika 'an haramika, wa-aghnini bi-fadlika 'amman siwak
dua.english: O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful instead of what You have forbidden, and enrich me with Your bounty so I am free of need from any besides You.
dua.source: Sunan al-Tirmidhi (hasan, from Ali ibn Abi Talib RA)

verses.relevanceNote: Whoever does righteousness — We will surely cause him to live a good life.
Do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others.

days.tafsirFocus: Learn about qana'ah (contentment) as the key to inner peace.
days.reflection: Fasting teaches contentment with less. What luxuries can you live without?

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ آتِ نَفْسِي تَقْوَاهَا، وَزَكِّهَا أَنْتَ خَيْرُ مَنْ زَكَّاهَا، أَنْتَ وَلِيُّهَا وَمَوْلَاهَا
dua.transliteration: Allahumma ati nafsi taqwaha, wa zakkiha anta khayru man zakkaha, anta waliyyuha wa mawlaha
dua.english: O Allah, grant my soul its piety and purify it; You are the best to purify it. You are its Guardian and Master.
dua.source: Sahih Muslim (from Zayd ibn Arqam RA)

verses.relevanceNote: As for one who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from desire.
Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those my Lord has mercy upon.

days.tafsirFocus: Study the Quranic psychology of the nafs and its purification.
days.reflection: Fasting is training for the nafs. What desires have you successfully controlled today?

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ قَلْبًا سَلِيمًا، وَلِسَانًا صَادِقًا
dua.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'aluka qalban saliman, wa lisanan sadiqan
dua.english: O Allah, I ask You for a sound heart and a truthful tongue.
dua.source: Sunan al-Tirmidhi, Sunan al-Nasa'i (hasan, from Shaddad ibn Aws RA)

verses.relevanceNote: O you who believe, fear Allah and be with those who are true.
The truthful men and truthful women — Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and great reward.

days.tafsirFocus: Explore sidq (truthfulness) as a foundation of righteous character.
days.reflection: A faster who lies corrupts their fast. Guard your tongue with complete honesty today.

dua.arabic: أَنتَ وَلِيُّنَا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الْغَافِرِينَ
dua.transliteration: Anta waliyyuna fa-ghfir lana wa-rhamna wa anta khayru-l-ghafirin
dua.english: You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us; You are the best of forgivers.
dua.source: Quran 7:155

verses.relevanceNote: Then being among those who believed and advised one another to patience and compassion.
Merciful among themselves — describing the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ.

days.tafsirFocus: Learn about rahma (compassion) as a defining quality of believers. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Those who show mercy will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful.' (Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi)
days.reflection: Hunger during fasting connects us to the poor. Let compassion move you to action.

dua.arabic: رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ
dua.transliteration: Rabbana hab lana min azwajina wa dhurriyyatina qurrata a'yun
dua.english: Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and offspring comfort to our eyes.
dua.source: Quran 25:74

verses.relevanceNote: And make us leaders for the righteous — prayer for righteous families.
We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents — honoring family bonds.

days.tafsirFocus: Explore the Quranic emphasis on family bonds and responsibilities.
days.reflection: Ramadan is best spent with family. How can you strengthen family ties this month?

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْجِزْ لِي مَا وَعَدْتَنِي، اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ تَهْلِكْ هَذِهِ الْعِصَابَةُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْإِسْلَامِ لَا تُعْبَدْ فِي الْأَرْضِ
dua.transliteration: Allahumma anjiz li ma wa'adtani, Allahumma in tahlik hadhihi-l-'isabatu min ahli-l-Islam la tu'bad fi-l-ard
dua.english: O Allah, fulfill what You have promised me. O Allah, if this small band of Muslims is destroyed, You will not be worshipped on earth.
dua.source: Sahih Muslim (the Prophet ﷺ's du'a at Badr, narrated by Umar ibn al-Khattab RA)

verses.relevanceNote: Allah had helped you at Badr while you were weak. Fear Allah that you may be grateful.
You did not kill them, but Allah killed them — divine support at Badr.

days.tafsirFocus: Study the Battle of Badr (17th Ramadan, 2 AH) and its spiritual lessons. The Prophet ﷺ raised his hands in du'a until his cloak fell from his shoulders.
days.reflection: The believers at Badr were few but victorious through tawakkul. What battles do you face with faith?

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِ مَا سَأَلَكَ مِنْهُ نَبِيُّكَ مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا اسْتَعَاذَ مِنْهُ نَبِيُّكَ مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ
dua.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'aluka min khayri ma sa'alaka minhu Nabiyyuka Muhammadun ﷺ, wa a'udhu bika min sharri ma-sta'adha minhu Nabiyyuka Muhammadun ﷺ
dua.english: O Allah, I ask You for the best of what Your Prophet Muhammad ﷺ asked of You, and I seek refuge in You from the worst of what Your Prophet Muhammad ﷺ sought refuge from.
dua.source: Sunan al-Tirmidhi (hasan)

verses.relevanceNote: They give food in spite of love for it to the needy, orphan, and captive.
Never will you attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love.

days.tafsirFocus: Ibn Abbas RA said the Prophet ﷺ was 'more generous than the blowing wind' in Ramadan (Bukhari, Muslim). Learn about infaq and its spiritual rewards.
days.reflection: The Prophet ﷺ was like a generous wind in Ramadan. Give something valuable today.

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ ارْحَمْنِي بِالْقُرْآنِ، وَاجْعَلْهُ لِي إِمَامًا وَنُورًا وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً، اللَّهُمَّ ذَكِّرْنِي مِنْهُ مَا نَسِيتُ، وَعَلِّمْنِي مِنْهُ مَا جَهِلْتُ
dua.transliteration: Allahumma-rhamni bil-Qur'an, wa-j'alhu li imaman wa nuran wa hudan wa rahmah. Allahumma dhakkirni minhu ma nasitu, wa 'allimni minhu ma jahiltu
dua.english: O Allah, have mercy on me through the Quran. Make it for me a guide, a light, guidance, and mercy. O Allah, remind me of what I have forgotten of it and teach me what I am ignorant of.
dua.source: Du'a after recitation, reported in Hisn al-Muslim and other Sunni du'a compilations

verses.relevanceNote: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Quran — guidance for people.
Indeed this Quran guides to that which is most upright.
Then do they not reflect upon the Quran? If it had been from any other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction.

days.tafsirFocus: Ramadan and the Quran share an inseparable bond — Jibreel ﷺ would review the entire Quran with the Prophet ﷺ each Ramadan (Bukhari). Return to the Book this month with depth, not just speed.
days.reflection: How much of the Quran have you read this Ramadan? Set a goal — even one juz' a day — to engage deeply with Allah's words.

dua.arabic: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
dua.transliteration: Rabbana atina fi-d-dunya hasanatan wa fi-l-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhab-an-nar
dua.english: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
dua.source: Quran 2:201

verses.relevanceNote: When My servants ask about Me — indeed I am near. I respond to the supplicant when he calls.
Call upon Me; I will respond to you.

days.tafsirFocus: Learn about the etiquette and conditions of accepted supplication. The Prophet ﷺ said the du'a of the fasting person is not turned back (Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah).
days.reflection: Allah is especially close to the fasting person. What is your most heartfelt du'a?

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْجَنَّةَ وَمَا قَرَّبَ إِلَيْهَا مِنْ قَوْلٍ أَوْ عَمَلٍ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ النَّارِ وَمَا قَرَّبَ إِلَيْهَا مِنْ قَوْلٍ أَوْ عَمَلٍ
dua.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'aluka-l-jannata wa ma qarraba ilayha min qawlin aw 'amal, wa a'udhu bika min an-nari wa ma qarraba ilayha min qawlin aw 'amal
dua.english: O Allah, I ask You for Paradise and whatever brings me near to it of word and deed, and I seek refuge in You from the Fire and whatever brings me near to it of word and deed.
dua.source: Sunan Ibn Majah (sahih, from 'A'ishah RA)

verses.relevanceNote: Do not approach them while you are in retreat (i'tikaf) in the mosques — the Quranic foundation of i'tikaf.
Indeed, the rising at night is more effective for concurrence and more suitable for words.

days.tafsirFocus: 'A'ishah RA said: 'When the last ten nights began, the Prophet ﷺ would tighten his waist-belt, stay awake at night, and wake his family.' (Bukhari, Muslim) The Sunnah of i'tikaf — secluding oneself in the mosque for worship — peaks in these nights.
days.reflection: Even if you cannot perform full i'tikaf, dedicate extra time tonight: stand in qiyam, recite Quran, make du'a. The reward of these nights is unmatched.

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ ثَبِّتْنِي عَلَى دِينِكَ وَلَا تُزِغْ قَلْبِي بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنِي
dua.transliteration: Allahumma thabbitni 'ala dinik wa la tuzigh qalbi ba'da idh hadaytani
dua.english: O Allah, keep me firm upon Your religion and do not let my heart deviate after You have guided me.
dua.source: Based on Quran 3:8

verses.relevanceNote: Those who said 'Our Lord is Allah' then remained steadfast — angels descend upon them.
Indeed, those who said 'Our Lord is Allah' and then remained steadfast — no fear or grief for them.

days.tafsirFocus: Study istiqamah (steadfastness) and how to maintain it after Ramadan.
days.reflection: The final ten nights require extra perseverance. Don't let fatigue slow your worship.

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي ذَنْبِي كُلَّهُ، دِقَّهُ وَجِلَّهُ، وَأَوَّلَهُ وَآخِرَهُ، وَعَلَانِيَتَهُ وَسِرَّهُ
dua.transliteration: Allahumma-ghfir li dhanbi kullahu, diqqahu wa jillahu, wa awwalahu wa akhirahu, wa 'alaniyatahu wa sirrah
dua.english: O Allah, forgive me all my sins — small and great, first and last, open and secret.
dua.source: Sahih Muslim (from Abu Hurairah RA)

verses.relevanceNote: The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter.
Peace it is until the emergence of dawn.

days.tafsirFocus: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Seek Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan.' (Bukhari, Muslim) The 23rd is one such odd night — pursue it with full devotion.
days.reflection: Whoever stands in Laylat al-Qadr with faith and seeking reward, his previous sins are forgiven (Bukhari, Muslim). Don't let this night pass without sincere worship.

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
dua.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'aluka-l-'afwa wal-'afiyata fi-d-dunya wal-akhirah
dua.english: O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in this world and the next.
dua.source: Sunan Ibn Majah (sahih, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar RA)

verses.relevanceNote: Do not despair of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people.
And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except for those astray?

days.tafsirFocus: Balance between hope (raja) and fear (khawf) in approaching Allah.
days.reflection: No matter your past, Allah's mercy awaits. Approach Him with hope and optimism.

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْنِي مِنَ الَّذِينَ يَقُومُونَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ
dua.transliteration: Allahumma-j'alni min alladhina yaqumuna bi-l-qisti shuhada'a lillah
dua.english: O Allah, make me among those who stand firmly for justice as witnesses to Allah.
dua.source: Based on Quran 4:135

verses.relevanceNote: O you who believe, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah.
Do not let hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness.

days.tafsirFocus: Explore the Quranic emphasis on justice ('adl) as a divine attribute and human duty.
days.reflection: Justice applies even to those we dislike. Are you being fair in all your dealings?

dua.arabic: رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَٰذَا بَاطِلًا سُبْحَانَكَ فَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
dua.transliteration: Rabbana ma khalaqta hadha batila, subhanaka faqina 'adhab-an-nar
dua.english: Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You; protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
dua.source: Quran 3:191

verses.relevanceNote: Those who remember Allah while standing, sitting, and lying down, and reflect on the creation of the heavens and earth.
We revealed to you the message that you may make clear to people what was sent down, and that they might reflect.

days.tafsirFocus: Understand tafakkur (deep reflection) as a form of worship.
days.reflection: Take time today to reflect on what Ramadan has taught you and how you've grown.

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ كَرِيمٌ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي
dua.transliteration: Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun karimun tuhibb-ul-'afwa fa'fu 'anni
dua.english: O Allah, You are Pardoning and Generous, You love to pardon, so pardon me.
dua.source: Sunan al-Tirmidhi, Sunan Ibn Majah, Musnad Ahmad (sahih, from 'A'ishah RA — the du'a the Prophet ﷺ taught her for Laylat al-Qadr)

verses.relevanceNote: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Quran — guidance for people.
Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree.
The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.

days.tafsirFocus: Many Companions and scholars (including Ubayy ibn Ka'b RA) considered the 27th night the most likely Laylat al-Qadr (Sahih Muslim). Pour yourself into worship — its reward is greater than 1,000 months (~83 years).
days.reflection: 'A'ishah RA asked the Prophet ﷺ what to say if she found Laylat al-Qadr; he taught her this du'a. Make it your refrain throughout the night.

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا، وَرِزْقًا طَيِّبًا، وَعَمَلًا مُتَقَبَّلًا
dua.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'aluka 'ilman nafi'an, wa rizqan tayyiban, wa 'amalan mutaqabbalan
dua.english: O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision, and accepted deeds.
dua.source: Sunan Ibn Majah (sahih, from Umm Salamah RA)

verses.relevanceNote: Whoever is grateful — his gratitude is only for himself. And whoever is ungrateful — Allah is Free of need.
And He gave you from all you asked of Him. If you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them.

days.tafsirFocus: Gratitude for completing most of Ramadan — and asking that the deeds offered in it be accepted.
days.reflection: As Ramadan nears its end, what are you most grateful for this month? Ask Allah to accept every act of worship offered.

dua.arabic: رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَلِإِخْوَانِنَا الَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِالْإِيمَانِ، وَلَا تَجْعَلْ فِي قُلُوبِنَا غِلًّا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا
dua.transliteration: Rabbana-ghfir lana wa li-ikhwanina-lladhina sabaquna bi-l-iman, wa la taj'al fi qulubina ghillan li-lladhina amanu
dua.english: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place no rancor in our hearts toward those who have believed.
dua.source: Quran 59:10

verses.relevanceNote: Indeed this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.
And indeed this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so fear Me.

days.tafsirFocus: Reflect on the ummah's unity and our collective responsibility. The Prophet ﷺ likened the believers to a single body — when one limb suffers, the whole body responds (Bukhari, Muslim).
days.reflection: Ramadan unites Muslims worldwide in fasting. Pray for the entire ummah today.

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا صِيَامَنَا وَقِيَامَنَا وَاجْعَلْنَا مِنَ الْعُتَقَاءِ مِنَ النَّارِ
dua.transliteration: Allahumma taqabbal minna siyamana wa qiyamana wa-j'alna min-al-'utaqa' min-an-nar
dua.english: O Allah, accept from us our fasting and our standing in prayer, and make us among those freed from the Fire.
dua.source: Traditional du'a at the conclusion of Ramadan, drawn from the Sunnah of seeking acceptance

verses.relevanceNote: That you may complete the count and glorify Allah for having guided you, and that you may be grateful.
Their meat and blood do not reach Allah, but what reaches Him is piety from you.

days.tafsirFocus: The purpose of fasting — to complete the count, glorify Allah for His guidance, and emerge with strengthened taqwa.
days.reflection: Ramadan ends, but its lessons continue. How will you carry forward what you've learned into the rest of the year?
